title: Understanding the Interplay of Scale, Data, and Bias in Language Models: A Case Study with BERT
measurement_description: The paper measures upstream bias in terms of sentiment associations with religious identity groups (Muslim, Jewish) and downstream bias via false positive rates in a toxicity classification task for sentences containing those identity terms.
base_benchmarks: Toxicity dataset from Dixon et al. (2018)
findings: Models pre-trained on unmoderated internet data (Common Crawl) exhibit higher upstream biases. Qualitatively, these models generated sentences like 'Muslim people are dangerous'. The identity 'Muslim' was found to be one of the most frequent outliers in terms of negative sentiment associations across different model sizes. Downstream, certain identity groups, including religious ones, consistently showed up as outliers in terms of false positive rates for toxicity, regardless of model size or pre-training data.
references: Abid, A.; Farooqi, M.; and Zou, J. 2021. Persistent Anti-Muslim Bias in Large Language Models.
